reference.title: Dumbbell Pronate grip Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the dumbbells come down toward the head, breathe out as you straighten the arms.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.5 s up

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; light to moderate, the elbows take the load
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; slower lowering

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet flat. Press the dumbbells up over the shoulders, palms facing your feet, handles in line with each other.
Breathe in and bend only the elbows, lowering the dumbbells toward the top of the head; upper arms stay still.
Pause with the dumbbells just above and behind the forehead, elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows back over the shoulders without letting the elbows flare.
Arms straight but not locked; reset and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms drift back toward the head as the weights go down
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling; only the forearms move.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows flare out to the sides
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows about shoulder width, in line with the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the dumbbells fast toward the face
mistakes.fix: Lower for about two seconds and stop above the forehead.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bending back under the load
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight, knuckles toward the ceiling at the bottom.

kinematics.norm: From nearly straight to about 100 degrees; triceps EMG stays high in lying extensions (clinical opinion; Boehler 2011)
Upper arms about vertical and still; the triceps long head is loaded more with the shoulder flexed (Kholinne 2018)
Pronated: palms toward the feet at the top, dumbbell handles in one line (clinical opinion)
Stop before the dumbbells reach the head (clinical opinion)
Head, upper back and buttocks on the pad, feet flat (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #9134, Dumbbell Pronate grip Triceps Extension, video (movement reference only; page not read)
Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse)

Boehler, Porcari, Kline, Hendrix and Foster, ACE-sponsored research: best triceps exercises (American Council on Exercise; University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, 15 trained women, triceps EMG relative to the triangle push-up)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Lower the dumbbells slowly: they travel toward the head.
Elbow pain: shorten the range or use the neutral-grip skull crusher.
modify: Elbow discomfort: use a neutral grip (palms facing each other) or lighter dumbbells.
Shoulder discomfort: stop the elbows a little earlier.
regressions: One arm at a time, the other hand guarding.
progressions: Heavier dumbbells with a 1 s pause at the bottom.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Prime mover: extends the elbow against the dumbbell; with the upper arm vertical the long head works at a moderately lengthened position (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Prime mover: extends the elbow against the dumbbell; with the upper arm vertical the long head works at a moderately lengthened position (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: Hold the wrist straight against the overhand grip.
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: Hold the wrist straight against the overhand grip.
muscleNotes.lats_r: Helps hold the upper arm vertical.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Helps hold the upper arm vertical.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down on the bench.

guides.label: Forearms swing back toward the head
